subtopics.title: Why Equations Must Balance — Conservation of Mass

questions.question: The law of conservation of mass states that in a chemical reaction:
options: Atoms are neither created nor destroyed — only rearranged
Mass slowly decreases as gas escapes
Products always weigh more than reactants
Energy and mass are the same thing

questions.question: In the unbalanced equation C3H8 + O2 → CO2 + H2O, what is wrong?
options: The atom counts differ across the arrow — it claims atoms vanished and appeared
The arrow points the wrong way

questions.question: In the combustion of propane, the fuel's carbon and hydrogen atoms leave as:
options: They are destroyed by the flame

subtopics.title: The One Commandment — Coefficients, Never Subscripts

questions.question: Why is changing H2O to H2O2 an illegal balancing move?
options: Editing a subscript changes the substance — H2O2 is hydrogen peroxide, not water
It is legal when oxygen needs balancing
Subscripts may only change on the left side

questions.question: How many hydrogen and oxygen atoms are in 4H2O?
options: 8 hydrogens and 4 oxygens — the coefficient multiplies every atom in the formula

questions.question: For combustion equations, the recommended balancing order is:
options: Carbon, then hydrogen, then oxygen last
Oxygen first because there is most of it

questions.question: Why is oxygen balanced LAST in combustion?
options: It appears in both products and stands alone as O2, so its count depends on the other coefficients

subtopics.title: Balancing the Propane Equation — C, then H, then O

questions.question: The balanced propane equation is:
The oxygen coefficient of 5 comes from:
options: Counting 6 + 4 = 10 oxygen atoms needed on the right, supplied in pairs: 10 ÷ 2 = 5

questions.question: The closing audit of the balanced equation checks:
options: Every element's atom count on both sides: C 3=3, H 8=8, O 10=10
That the coefficients add up to 13

subtopics.title: Fractions, Final Form, and the Road to Stoichiometry

questions.question: Balancing ethane (C2H6) lands on 7/2 O2. The Grade 10 convention is to:
options: Leave the fraction as the final answer
Change a subscript to absorb the half

questions.question: Why is 2C3H8 + 10O2 → 6CO2 + 8H2O not an acceptable final answer?
options: Every coefficient divides by 2 — the final form must use the smallest whole-number set

questions.question: Next term, the coefficients 1 : 5 : 3 : 4 become:
options: Mole ratios — one mole of propane reacts with five moles of oxygen
The masses of each substance in grams

questions.question: Which step is NEVER optional at the end of balancing?
options: The element-by-element audit proving both sides match

subtopics.title: Nothing Goes Missing at the Braai

questions.question: Weighing the gas and air that go into a braai flame against everything that leaves shows that:
options: The two piles weigh exactly the same — atoms are taken apart and reassembled, never burned away
The products weigh less, because gas is lost
The products weigh more, because fire adds mass
Nothing measurable can be said about the masses

questions.question: In the braai flame, every carbon in the propane ends up in:
options: The carbon dioxide going up in the heat haze

questions.question: The unbalanced first attempt is wrong because:
options: Water is not a real product
Our COUNTING is wrong — two carbons and six hydrogens go missing and an oxygen appears from nowhere

questions.question: "What goes in the bag comes out of the bag" is the shop version of:
options: The law of conservation of mass

subtopics.title: Buy More Packets, Don't Repack Them

questions.question: The BIG number written in front of a formula:
options: Is the number of packets — change it freely, since the substance itself stays the same
Is part of the substance's label and may not be changed
Applies only to the first atom in the formula
Must always be a whole number greater than one

questions.question: Changing H2O to H2O2 to make the oxygens balance is illegal because:
options: It swaps the PRODUCT — hydrogen peroxide is wound-cleaning liquid, not water, so the equation describes a reaction that never happened
Subscripts may only be increased, never decreased
It makes the equation too long

questions.question: Four H2O contains:
options: EIGHT hydrogens and four oxygens — the big number multiplies everything in the packet

questions.question: A formula written with no big number in front:
options: Is being ignored in the count
Means the substance is a product
Carries an invisible one — like a single loaf on the counter still being one loaf

subtopics.title: Easy Ones First, Then the Awkward One

questions.question: Oxygen is balanced LAST when burning a fuel because:
options: It appears in BOTH products, so sorting it first means every later change breaks it again

questions.question: After placing three carbon dioxides and four waters, the oxygen demand is:
options: TEN atoms — six from the three carbon dioxides plus four from the four waters — so five oxygen pairs

questions.question: Burning ethane needs three and a half oxygen pairs. The honest fix is to:
options: Leave the fraction in the final answer
DOUBLE the whole shopping list — two ethane, seven oxygen, four carbon dioxide, six water
Change a subscript to remove the half

questions.question: The final check that turns hoping into knowing is:
options: Counting BOTH sides out loud — carbons, hydrogens and oxygens each matching
